To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

an anti‐CD18 mAb treatment reduces macrophage and neutrophil infiltration into the spinal cord lesion, reduces lipid peroxidative damage and nitrotylosine formation, and improves functional recovery after SCI.
an anti‐CD18 mAb treatment reduces macrophage, neutrophil, and reactive oxygen and nitrogen‐species production, and improves neurological function after spinal cord injury.
an anti‐CD18 mAb treatment reduces macrophage infiltration and neutrophil infiltration, lipid peroxidation (TBARS) and protein nitration in the spinal cord after severe clip‐compressed SCI in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role played by leukocyte integrins in the pathophysiology of SCI and the development of new therapeutic strategies for SCI based on the blockade of leukocyte integrin function.
the mechanisms of anti‐CD11 integrin antibody‐induced protection in the injured spinal cord, with particular attention to the anti‐inflammatory effects of the treatment.

the role of the leukocyte adhesion receptor CD11d in the pathogenesis of secondary tissue damage following SCI and the potential of anti‐CD11 antibodies to improve functional recovery after SCI in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mAb treatment reduces the intraspinal concentration of reactive oxygen and reactive nitrogen species, and that this effect may contribute to the improved neurological outcome observed in the anti‐CD11/18 mAb‐treated animals after SCI.

the CD11d mAb is a novel therapeutic agent for SCI that is effective in blocking neutrophil and monocyte/macrophage trafficking and infiltration, reducing the formation of reactive oxygen and reactive nitrogen species and thereby improving tissue preservation and neurological outcome after SCI.
the anti‐CD11 mAb treatment reduces lipid peroxides and protein nitration and improves neurological outcome after SCI in rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anti‐CD 11d mAb therapy is a promising treatment for SCI, and that this treatment is associated with decreased intraspinal inflammation and reduced tissue damage.
the anti‐CD11/CD18 mAb treatment attenuates intraspinal oxidative and nitrative stress and preserves neurological function after severe SCI.
anti‐CD18 mAbs reduce neutrophil infiltration and macrophage activation in the injured spinal cord.
The main takeaway from our work is that
anti‐CD 11d mAb therapy reduces intraspinal neutro‐ and macrophage accumulation, lipid peroxidation (TBARS) and protein nitration (nitrotyrosine) after SCI.
anti‐CD18 antibody treatment reduces macrophage and neutrophil infiltration, lipid peroxidation (TBARS), nitrotyrosination, and inducible nitrosynthase (iNOST) after spinal cord injury.
the anti‐CD11/18 integrin mAb treatment reduces the intraspinal concentration of reactive oxygen and reactive nitrogen species after SCI, likely contributing to improved neurological function.
